title: Audit Report
health_method: This score measures source code security only. Formula: 100 ÷ (1 + P ÷ (20 × F)), where P = sum of penalties and F = LOC factor (lines of code ÷ 1,000, minimum 1). Each Security finding costs: CRITICAL (10), HIGH (5), MEDIUM (2), LOW (1). LOC weighting normalizes the score by project size. Non-security categories (Architecture, UI, UX, Maintenance) are not factored in.
top_files_subtitle: Ranked by severity score (CRITICAL×10, HIGH×5, MEDIUM×2, LOW×1)
severity_distribution_subtitle: Number of issues per severity level (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, INFO)
by_category_subtitle: Number of issues per audit category (Security, Architecture, UI, UX, Maintenance) — not to be confused with severity above
category_examples_subtitle: The most frequent issue in each category, with a real instance detected in this project and the generic fix for this type of pattern.
category_example_fix: How to fix this type of pattern
category_example_bridge: 💡 This rule flags a broader principle than just this snippet: {solution}. The example below illustrates the general fix principle, not necessarily your exact case.

chart_subtitles.database_history: Tables, columns and changes over 10 audits

validations_intro: This section lists positive findings from the audit. Each item represents a verified security or architecture good practice in your code.
success_cat_no_critical: {cat}: no CRITICAL or HIGH finding — category within acceptable thresholds.
success_fixtures_coverage: Fixture coverage: {rate}% — all rules validated by test cases.
no_issues_category: No issues detected in this category.

fixtures_some_incorrect: Some fixtures are not correctly detected
fixtures_explanation: Each detection rule is tested against two types of test files (fixtures): vulnerable fixtures contain a known security pattern and must trigger a detection, while clean fixtures contain safe code and must not trigger any alert. This section measures the reliability of every rule.
fixtures_true_positives_desc: Vulnerable fixtures correctly detected by the rule
fixtures_true_negatives_desc: Clean fixtures correctly ignored (no false alert)
fixtures_false_negatives_desc: Vulnerable fixtures missed by the rule (detection failure)
deps_warn_no_distribution: Dependency incompatible with the audit .venv Python version. CVE scan was interrupted.
deps_warn_no_distribution_fix: Update the dependency to a compatible version, or run pip-audit with a Python version compatible with the project.
deps_warn_timeout_fix: Check your network connection or reduce the number of dependencies.
deps_warn_tool_missing_fix: Install the indicated tool to enable CVE scanning.
deps_warn_generic_fix: Check the dependency file and rerun the audit.

hardcoded_secret.name: Hardcoded secret
hardcoded_secret.risk: Plain text secrets in code can be exposed via Git repository.
hardcoded_secret.solution: Use environment variables or system_configs in database.

weak_crypto.name: Weak cryptographic algorithm
weak_crypto.risk: MD5 and SHA1 are vulnerable to collisions and must not be used for secure hashing.
weak_crypto.solution: Use SHA-256/SHA-512 for hashing, bcrypt/argon2 for passwords.
weak_crypto.benefit: Resistance to collision and brute-force attacks (CWE-328).

insecure_random.name: Insecure RNG
insecure_random.risk: Math.random() is predictable and must not be used for tokens, OTPs or keys.
insecure_random.solution: Use crypto.getRandomValues() or crypto.randomUUID() for sensitive values.
insecure_random.benefit: Unpredictable tokens and keys, resistant to attacks (CWE-330).

img_no_alt.name: Image without alt text
img_no_alt.risk: Images without alternative text are inaccessible to screen readers and visually impaired users.
img_no_alt.solution: Add a descriptive alt attribute on every tag.

focus_outline_removed.name: Focus outline removed
focus_outline_removed.risk: Removing the outline prevents keyboard users from seeing which element has focus.
focus_outline_removed.solution: Do not remove outline. If the default style is unsuitable, replace it with a visible alternative.
focus_outline_removed.benefit: WCAG 2.4.7 compliance — focus always visible for keyboard navigation.

unpinned_action_version.name: Unpinned action version
unpinned_action_version.risk: Referencing actions by mutable tag (v1, main) exposes the pipeline to tag-hijacking supply chain attacks.
unpinned_action_version.solution: Pin actions to a full commit SHA (40 hex chars). Add a comment with the version for readability.
unpinned_action_version.benefit: Immunity against tag-hijacking attacks like the Codecov/tj-actions incidents (OWASP CI-CD-09).

hardcoded_secret_cicd.name: Hardcoded secret in CI/CD configuration
hardcoded_secret_cicd.risk: A secret value (password, token, API key) is hardcoded directly in the CI/CD configuration file and exposed to all repository contributors.
hardcoded_secret_cicd.solution: Move secrets to your CI/CD platform's secret store (GitHub Secrets, GitLab CI Variables) and reference them via environment variables.
hardcoded_secret_cicd.benefit: Eliminates credential exposure in version control history and CI/CD logs (OWASP CI-CD-04, CWE-798).

docker_latest_tag.name: Docker image with :latest tag
docker_latest_tag.risk: Using the :latest Docker image tag in CI/CD pipelines causes unpredictable builds as the referenced image may change without notice.
docker_latest_tag.solution: Pin Docker images to a specific version tag or digest (e.g., node:20.11-alpine or node@sha256:...).
docker_latest_tag.benefit: Ensures reproducible and secure builds by preventing silent image upgrades in the CI/CD pipeline.

ci_docker_privileged.name: Privileged Docker container in CI/CD
ci_docker_privileged.risk: Running a CI/CD container with privileged mode grants full access to the host kernel, devices, and namespaces — equivalent to root on the host system.
ci_docker_privileged.solution: Remove the --privileged flag. Use specific Linux capabilities (--cap-add) only for exact functionality required.
ci_docker_privileged.benefit: Prevents container escape attacks and limits blast radius of a compromised CI/CD job to the container.

unsafe_deserialization_java.name: Unsafe deserialization (Java)
unsafe_deserialization_java.risk: ObjectInputStream.readObject() without validation allows arbitrary code running.
unsafe_deserialization_java.solution: Use ObjectInputFilter (Java 9+) or a whitelist of allowed classes. Prefer JSON/XML serialization.
unsafe_deserialization_java.benefit: Protection against deserialization attacks (OWASP A08, CWE-502).

weak_crypto_java.name: Weak cryptography (Java)
weak_crypto_java.risk: MD5 and SHA-1 are cryptographically broken — vulnerable to collision attacks.
weak_crypto_java.solution: Use SHA-256 or SHA-3 (MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256")). For passwords, use BCrypt/Argon2.

weak_random_java.name: Weak random (Java)
weak_random_java.risk: java.util.Random is predictable — tokens, sessions, and keys generated with it can be guessed.
weak_random_java.solution: Use java.security.SecureRandom for all security-sensitive random generation.

unsafe_deserialization_csharp.name: Unsafe deserialization (C#)
unsafe_deserialization_csharp.risk: BinaryFormatter and TypeNameHandling.All allow arbitrary code running via crafted payloads.
unsafe_deserialization_csharp.solution: Use System.Text.Json or Newtonsoft.Json with TypeNameHandling.None. Never use BinaryFormatter (CA2300).
unsafe_deserialization_csharp.benefit: Protection against deserialization attacks (OWASP A08, CWE-502, SCS0028).

weak_crypto_csharp.name: Weak cryptography (C#)
weak_crypto_csharp.risk: MD5, SHA1, DES, TripleDES and ECB mode are cryptographically broken.
weak_crypto_csharp.solution: Use SHA256, SHA512, or AES-GCM. For passwords, use BCrypt/Argon2/PBKDF2.
weak_crypto_csharp.benefit: Strong cryptographic operations (OWASP A02, CWE-328, SCS0006/CA5350).

weak_random_csharp.name: Weak random (C#)
weak_random_csharp.risk: System.Random is predictable — tokens, sessions, and keys generated with it can be guessed.
weak_random_csharp.solution: Use RandomNumberGenerator (System.Security.Cryptography) for security-sensitive random generation.
weak_random_csharp.benefit: Unpredictable token/key generation (OWASP A02, CWE-330, SCS0005).

unsafe_deserialization_php.name: Unsafe deserialization (PHP)
unsafe_deserialization_php.risk: unserialize() with untrusted data allows PHP Object Injection attacks.
unsafe_deserialization_php.solution: Use json_decode() instead. If unserialize is required, use allowed_classes option.
unsafe_deserialization_php.benefit: Protection against object injection attacks (OWASP A08, CWE-502).

insecure_cookie.name: Insecure cookie (missing HttpOnly/Secure)
insecure_cookie.risk: Cookies without HttpOnly are accessible via JavaScript (XSS). Without Secure, they are sent over unencrypted HTTP (CWE-614, OWASP A05).
insecure_cookie.solution: Always set HttpOnly=True and Secure=True on session and authentication cookies.
insecure_cookie.benefit: Cookies protected against XSS theft and network interception.

weak_crypto_php.name: Weak cryptography (PHP)
weak_crypto_php.risk: md5()/sha1() are cryptographically broken — vulnerable to collision and rainbow table attacks.
weak_crypto_php.solution: Use password_hash() with PASSWORD_BCRYPT or PASSWORD_ARGON2ID for passwords.

weak_random_php.name: Weak random (PHP)
weak_random_php.risk: rand()/mt_rand() are predictable — tokens and keys generated with them can be guessed.
weak_random_php.solution: Use random_bytes() or random_int() for security-sensitive random generation.

missing_mfa_python.name: Missing MFA (Python)
missing_mfa_python.risk: Authentication without multi-factor authentication exposes accounts to credential theft (CWE-308).
missing_mfa_python.solution: Integrate pyotp or django-otp for TOTP-based two-factor authentication.
missing_mfa_python.benefit: Stronger authentication, reduced risk of account compromise.

missing_mfa_java.name: Missing MFA (Java)
missing_mfa_java.risk: Authentication without multi-factor authentication exposes accounts to credential theft (CWE-308).
missing_mfa_java.solution: Integrate a TOTP library (dev.samstevens.totp, Google Authenticator) for two-factor authentication.
missing_mfa_java.benefit: Stronger authentication, reduced risk of account compromise.

missing_mfa_csharp.name: Missing MFA (C#)
missing_mfa_csharp.risk: Authentication without multi-factor authentication exposes accounts to credential theft (CWE-308).
missing_mfa_csharp.solution: Enable ASP.NET Identity TwoFactorSignInAsync or integrate a TOTP library.
missing_mfa_csharp.benefit: Stronger authentication, reduced risk of account compromise.

missing_mfa_javascript.name: Missing MFA (JavaScript)
missing_mfa_javascript.risk: Authentication without multi-factor authentication exposes accounts to credential theft (CWE-308).
missing_mfa_javascript.solution: Integrate speakeasy or otplib for TOTP-based two-factor authentication.
missing_mfa_javascript.benefit: Stronger authentication, reduced risk of account compromise.

missing_mfa_php.name: Missing MFA (PHP)
missing_mfa_php.risk: Authentication without multi-factor authentication exposes accounts to credential theft (CWE-308).
missing_mfa_php.solution: Integrate google2fa or pragmarx/google2fa-laravel for TOTP-based two-factor authentication.
missing_mfa_php.benefit: Stronger authentication, reduced risk of account compromise.

dockerfile_root_user.name: Dockerfile runs as root
dockerfile_root_user.risk: Container runs as root user by default, increasing blast radius if compromised (CWE-250).
dockerfile_root_user.solution: Add a USER directive with a non-root user (e.g., USER appuser) after installing dependencies.
dockerfile_root_user.benefit: Principle of least privilege, reduced container escape risk.

dockerfile_unpinned_base.name: Unpinned base image
dockerfile_unpinned_base.risk: Base image without version tag (FROM node) pulls latest, causing non-reproducible builds and potential supply chain issues.
dockerfile_unpinned_base.solution: Pin base image to a specific version or digest (e.g., FROM node:20-alpine or FROM node@sha256:...).
dockerfile_unpinned_base.benefit: Reproducible builds, protection against supply chain attacks.

dockerfile_copy_all.name: COPY . . in Dockerfile
dockerfile_copy_all.risk: COPY . . copies the entire build context including potential secrets (.env, credentials, SSH keys).
dockerfile_copy_all.solution: Use a .dockerignore file and copy only required files/directories explicitly.
dockerfile_copy_all.benefit: Smaller image, no accidental secret exposure in container layers.

missing_sri.name: Missing Subresource Integrity
missing_sri.risk: External scripts or stylesheets loaded without integrity attribute can be tampered with if the CDN is compromised (CWE-353).
missing_sri.solution: Add integrity attribute with SHA-256/384/512 hash and crossorigin='anonymous' to external script and link tags.
missing_sri.benefit: Ensures external resources have not been tampered with, protects against CDN compromise.

prototype_pollution.name: Prototype pollution
prototype_pollution.risk: Object.assign or __proto__ with user data allows modifying the global prototype and injecting properties (CWE-1321).
prototype_pollution.solution: Use Object.create(null) or Map, validate keys with a whitelist.
prototype_pollution.benefit: Protection against property injection on all objects.

inline_event_handler_html.name: Inline event handler in HTML
inline_event_handler_html.risk: on* attributes in HTML execute JavaScript directly, vulnerable to XSS (CWE-79).
inline_event_handler_html.solution: Move JavaScript to separate .js files with addEventListener().

html_no_lang.name: HTML missing lang attribute
html_no_lang.risk: Screen readers cannot determine the page language, affecting pronunciation.
html_no_lang.solution: Add lang attribute to the html element: <html lang="en">.
html_no_lang.benefit: Correct pronunciation for screen reader users.

missing_doctype.name: Missing DOCTYPE declaration
missing_doctype.risk: Browser renders in quirks mode, causing inconsistent layout and behavior.
missing_doctype.solution: Add <!DOCTYPE html> as the first line of the HTML document.

weak_random_python.name: Weak random number generator
weak_random_python.risk: random module is not cryptographically secure; predictable values enable attacks.
weak_random_python.solution: Use secrets module for security-sensitive operations: secrets.token_hex().
weak_random_python.benefit: Cryptographically secure random values for tokens and keys.

insecure_cookie_flag.name: Insecure Cookie Flag
insecure_cookie_flag.risk: Cookie with Secure flag set to false is transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections (CWE-614).
insecure_cookie_flag.solution: Set cookie.setSecure(true) to ensure cookies are only sent over HTTPS.
insecure_cookie_flag.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_codeinj.name: Taint Code Injection
taint_codeinj.risk: An attacker can execute arbitrary Python code on the server.
taint_codeinj.solution: Replace dynamic execution with ast.literal_eval() for data parsing, or use a whitelist of allowed operations.
taint_codeinj.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_deserialization.name: Taint Deserialization
taint_deserialization.risk: An attacker can achieve remote code execution by sending crafted serialized Java objects.
taint_deserialization.solution: Use ObjectInputFilter (Java 9+) or ValidatingObjectInputStream from Apache Commons.
taint_deserialization.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_ldap.name: Taint LDAP Injection
taint_ldap.risk: An attacker can modify LDAP queries to bypass authentication or extract data.
taint_ldap.solution: Use LdapEncoder.filterEncode() to sanitize input before LDAP queries.
taint_ldap.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_open_redirect.name: Taint Open Redirect
taint_open_redirect.risk: An attacker can redirect users to a malicious site via a crafted URL.
taint_open_redirect.solution: Validate redirect targets against an allowlist. Use url_for() for internal redirects.
taint_open_redirect.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_path_traversal.name: Taint Path Traversal
taint_path_traversal.risk: An attacker can read or write arbitrary files on the server.
taint_path_traversal.solution: Use path.basename() and validate the resolved path stays within the allowed directory.
taint_path_traversal.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_rce.name: Taint RCE
taint_rce.risk: An attacker can execute arbitrary commands.
taint_rce.solution: Avoid Runtime.exec with user input; use ProcessBuilder with argument lists.
taint_rce.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_sqli.name: Taint SQL Injection
taint_sqli.risk: An attacker can read, modify, or delete database records.
taint_sqli.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_xpathi.name: Taint XPath Injection
taint_xpathi.risk: An attacker can manipulate XPath queries to bypass authentication or extract XML data.
taint_xpathi.solution: Use parameterized XPath queries with variables parameter, or validate/escape user input.
taint_xpathi.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_xss.name: Taint XSS
taint_xss.risk: An attacker can inject malicious scripts that execute in other users' browsers.
taint_xss.solution: Escape all user input before rendering in HTML. Use framework auto-escaping or html.escape().
taint_xss.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_xxe.name: Taint XXE
taint_xxe.risk: An attacker can read local files, perform SSRF, or cause DoS via malicious XML.
taint_xxe.solution: Disable external entity processing: setFeature(DISALLOW_DOCTYPE, true).
taint_xxe.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

hardcoded_connection_string_java.name: Hardcoded DB credentials (Java)
hardcoded_connection_string_java.risk: A JDBC connection uses a hardcoded password literal or embedded credentials in the URL. Credentials in source code appear in version control history (CWE-798).
hardcoded_connection_string_java.solution: Read credentials from environment variables: System.getenv("DB_PASSWORD"). In Spring Boot, use ${DB_PASSWORD} in application.properties backed by environment variables.
hardcoded_connection_string_java.benefit: Prevents database credential exposure via source code and version control history (OWASP A02, CWE-798).

hardcoded_connection_string_php.name: Hardcoded DB credentials (PHP)
hardcoded_connection_string_php.risk: A database connection uses a hardcoded password literal as a direct argument to PDO, mysqli, or mysql_connect. Credentials in source code appear in version control history (CWE-798).
hardcoded_connection_string_php.solution: Read the password from environment variables: getenv('DB_PASSWORD'). Use vlucas/phpdotenv for .env files. Never commit .env files to version control.
hardcoded_connection_string_php.benefit: Prevents database credential exposure via source code and version control history (OWASP A02, CWE-798).

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.subtitle: Acronyms and technical terms used in this report.

aria.desc: HTML attributes that improve accessibility for assistive technologies.

asvs.desc: OWASP standard defining security requirements for web applications across 3 verification levels (L1/L2/L3).

cors.desc: Security mechanism controlling HTTP requests between different domains.

csp.desc: HTTP header restricting allowed content sources on a web page.

csrf.desc: Attack that forces an authenticated user to perform unwanted actions.

css.desc: Language for styling and formatting web pages.

cve.desc: Unique identifier for a known security vulnerability.

cvss.desc: Vulnerability severity rating system (score from 0 to 10).

cwe.desc: Standardized catalog of software weakness types.

dom.desc: Tree representation of an HTML document in memory.

dry.desc: Design principle that avoids code duplication.

gdpr.desc: European regulation on personal data protection.

html.desc: Markup language for structuring web pages.

http.desc: Web communication protocol. HTTPS adds encryption via TLS.

i18n.desc: Adapting software to support multiple languages and regions.

iso27001.desc: International standard for information security management systems (ISMS). Annex A defines 93 controls across 4 themes.

js.desc: Programming language primarily used for web development.

jwt.desc: Signed authentication token in JSON format, used for sessions.

md5.desc: Obsolete and insecure hashing algorithm — should no longer be used.

orm.desc: Abstraction layer between object code and relational databases.

owasp.desc: Global reference for web application security best practices.

rgpd.full: Règlement Général sur la Protection des Données
rgpd.desc: European data protection regulation (French name for GDPR).

sast.desc: Source code security analysis without running the application.

sca.desc: Abbreviation for StaticCodeAudit, the tool that generated this report.

sarif.desc: Standardized JSON format (OASIS) for exchanging static analysis results between tools and CI/CD systems.

sbom.desc: Comprehensive inventory of software components and dependencies in a project (CycloneDX format).

sha1.desc: Obsolete hashing algorithm — vulnerable to collision attacks.

ssrf.desc: Attack forcing a server to make requests to internal resources.

svg.desc: XML-based vector image format for the web.

tls.desc: Network communication encryption protocol (successor to SSL).

toctou.desc: Race condition vulnerability between checking and using a resource.

wcag.desc: W3C web accessibility guidelines — international standard.

xss.desc: Injection of malicious scripts into a web page viewed by other users.

cicd.desc: Automated pipeline that builds, tests and deploys code on every change.

cli.desc: Text-based interface used to interact with a program via a terminal.

fixture.desc: Code sample (vulnerable or clean) used to validate that a detection rule fires correctly.

hsts.desc: HTTP header that forces browsers to use HTTPS only, preventing downgrade attacks.

idor.desc: Access control flaw where an attacker can access resources by manipulating identifiers.

jndi.desc: Java API used for directory services; exploited in Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) for RCE.

ldap.desc: Protocol for accessing and maintaining directory services (user accounts, etc.).

mfa.desc: Authentication requiring two or more verification factors (password + OTP, etc.).

nosql.desc: Non-relational databases (MongoDB, Redis, etc.) vulnerable to injection if queries are unsanitised.

pii.desc: Any data that can identify an individual (name, email, SSN, etc.). Must be protected under GDPR.

rce.desc: Critical vulnerability allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary code on the server.

sla.desc: Commitment defining maximum resolution times per severity (e.g. CRITICAL: 24h, HIGH: 72h).

smtp.desc: Standard protocol for sending emails; injection vulnerabilities can allow email spoofing.

ssh.desc: Cryptographic protocol for secure remote access to servers.

ssl.desc: Deprecated predecessor of TLS. Its use indicates an outdated and insecure configuration.

ssti.desc: Injection of malicious code into a server-side template engine, potentially leading to RCE.

taint.desc: Data-flow tracking technique that follows untrusted input (source) to sensitive operations (sink) to detect injection vulnerabilities.

url.desc: Web address that identifies a resource on a network (e.g. https://example.com/path).

xml.desc: Structured data format widely used in configuration files, APIs, and document exchange.

xpath.desc: Query language for XML documents; injection can allow unauthorized data access.

xxe.desc: XML injection attack that exploits external entity processing to read files or trigger SSRF.

SECURITY.title: Security & OWASP
SECURITY.risk: Security vulnerabilities allow attackers to steal data, execute malicious code, or compromise the system.
SECURITY.solution: Use parameterized queries for SQL, textContent or a secure template system for DOM, and never hardcode secrets.
SECURITY.benefit: Immunity against SQL injections, XSS, and OWASP Top 10 compliance.

ARCH.title: Architecture & Patterns
ARCH.risk: Scattered business logic makes code difficult to test and causes duplication.
ARCH.solution: Centralize logic in Services, keep Routers minimal.
ARCH.benefit: Modular, testable code compliant with best practices.

UI.title: Interface & Rendering
UI.risk: Direct DOM manipulation is slow, insecure and makes debugging difficult.
UI.solution: Use a secure template system for all HTML rendering.
UI.benefit: Improved performance, XSS security, visual consistency.

UX.title: User Experience
UX.risk: Transient and untranslated notifications frustrate users and reduce accessibility.
UX.solution: Translate all user-facing text, make error messages persistent.
UX.benefit: Better accessibility, multi-language support, professional UX.

MAINTENANCE.title: Maintenance & DRY
MAINTENANCE.risk: Dead and duplicated code increases cognitive load and the risk of bugs.
MAINTENANCE.solution: Remove unused code, share common logic in modules.

DEPENDENCIES.title: Dependencies
DEPENDENCIES.risk: Vulnerable or unpinned dependencies expose the project to known attacks.
DEPENDENCIES.solution: Update vulnerable dependencies and pin exact versions.
DEPENDENCIES.benefit: Elimination of known CVEs, reproducible builds (OWASP A06).

DATABASE.title: PostgreSQL Schema
DATABASE.risk: Undetected schema changes can cause runtime errors.
DATABASE.solution: Check migrations, update code referencing modified elements.
DATABASE.benefit: Schema stability, early detection of breaking changes.

CICD.title: CI/CD Pipelines
CICD.risk: Misconfigured CI/CD pipelines expose the project to supply chain attacks.
CICD.solution: Pin actions by SHA, restrict permissions, validate triggers.
CICD.benefit: Protection against supply chain attacks (OWASP CI-CD Top 10).
